name: Fail-closed discrete epsilon-completion acceptance gate

statement.latest: \mathrm{ACCEPT}_\varepsilon(K)\;\Longleftarrow\;\delta_K+\beta_K\le\varepsilon;\qquad\text{if no proved }\beta_K\text{ is available, return HOLD rather than continuum-complete}
statement.note_ascii: ACCEPT_epsilon(K) only if delta_K + beta_K <= epsilon; without a proved omitted-information bound beta_K, HOLD for continuum-completeness

definitions.beta_K: proved computable upper bound on omitted information/tail, target PROP-EPSC-04
definitions.ACCEPT_epsilon: certification verdict at the declared tolerance
definitions.HOLD: fail-closed verdict when the hypotheses needed for certification are unavailable

parents.evidence: the acceptance rule consumes the measured nested-refinement defect
continuum/infinite-object certification requires a proved omitted-information upper bound; without it the rule explicitly returns HOLD

origin.source: Discrete epsilon-completion programme, 2026-09-10. Registered before implementation as a general certification protocol in Information Discrete Mathematics.

name: Computable omitted-information tail certificate target

statement.note_ascii: ||(I-P_K)x|| <= beta_K(R_K), beta_K >= 0, beta_K -> 0 as K -> infinity

definitions.R_K: finite records available at level K (notation here denotes the record set, not necessarily the restriction operator used in PROP-EPSC-01)
definitions.beta_K: computable upper bound derived only from declared finite records and stated assumptions
definitions.x: target object in the problem's declared completion space

parents.evidence: nested agreement does not control unrepresented distinctions; beta_K is the missing certificate needed to turn finite stability into an infinite-object guarantee
